question.problem: Consider the finite region bounded by the curve $x=y-2{y}^{2}$ and the $y$-axis. What integral gives the volume of the solid generated when that region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis?
question.worked_solution:
First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the $y$-axis by solving the following equation for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y-2{y}^{2} & =0 \\ y(1-2y) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $y=0$ and $y=\frac{1}{2}.$ So, we need to integrate from $y=0$ to $y=\frac{1}{2}.$

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{c}^{d}yf(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1/2}y(y-2{y}^{2})\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$
